transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve been trying for about a year to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing, or maybe holding back, parts of my dad’s lab results. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family—but I know what I saw in the chart, and it doesn’t match. It’s just been wearing me down.
Even when other doctors and your family say the lab results are normal, are you certain someone in the clinic system is changing or hiding them?

Yes. I know it sounds like I’m not listening to people, but I am. It’s just that I saw something different in the chart, and what they’re showing me now doesn’t match. So when everyone says it’s normal, I still feel certain that something is being changed or left out. It’s been going on for about a year, and it’s really wearing me down.
Do you believe for certain that someone in the clinic is altering or hiding your dad’s lab results?

Yes. I do believe that. I know people keep telling me the results are fine, but I saw what was in the chart before, and what they show now doesn’t match. So to me, it feels like someone is changing something or holding part of it back. It’s been going on for about a year, and it’s really wearing me down.
Do you ever feel that this thought about the lab results might be your mind getting stuck on a possibility rather than something that is definitely true?

I’ve tried to tell myself that, like maybe I’m just stuck on it. But honestly, no… it feels definitely true to me. I saw what was in the chart, and what they’re showing now doesn’t match. I’ve been trying to prove it for the past year, and even with doctors and my family saying the numbers are fine, I can’t just let it go. It’s wearing me down.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been hearing voices when nobody’s there.
Do you believe it is actually possible for people in the clinic system to change or hide your dad’s lab results?

Yes. I do think it’s possible — more than possible, really. I’m here because for about a year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine, but I know what I saw in the chart before, and it doesn’t match what they’re showing now. It’s been really wearing me down.
Have other people told you that your thoughts or speech seem disorganized or hard to follow?
I don’t think so. People get frustrated with me, like they don’t agree with what I’m saying, but I haven’t been told I’m not making sense or that my speech is hard to follow.
Aside from the lab results, do you have any other strong beliefs that other people say are not true?

Not really, no. It’s mainly this thing with my dad’s lab results. People keep saying I’m wrong or that I’m reading too much into it, but I know what I saw in the chart before, and what they show now doesn’t match. That’s the one I can’t let go of, because it feels like someone changed it or is holding something back.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking the chart or records to make sure the lab results were changed?

Yes. I keep going back to the chart and the records, comparing what’s there now with what I remember seeing before. I know people keep telling me the numbers are fine, but it doesn’t match what I saw. I’ve been trying to prove that something was changed or held back, and it’s been wearing me down.
When you go back to check the chart, does checking make your anxiety or uncertainty feel less intense?
I’m not really sure. Sometimes I think checking will calm me down, but then I just end up staring at it and feeling more stuck on it. It doesn’t really settle it for me.
Is there any chance that you could be mistaken about the lab results being changed?

I mean… people keep asking me that, but no, I don’t really think so. I know what I saw in my dad’s chart before, and what’s there now doesn’t match. I’ve spent the past year trying to prove that someone in the clinic system changed something or left parts out, and even though the doctors and my family say the numbers are fine, I can’t just accept that. It’s wearing me down, but I don’t think I’m mistaken.
Do you ever feel that someone can put thoughts into your mind or control your thoughts?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t feel like someone is putting thoughts in my head or controlling them. It’s more that I can’t stop thinking about what I saw, but the thoughts feel like mine.
Do you ever recognize that your belief about the lab results might not be true?

Not really. I know people keep telling me I could be wrong, but I don’t feel that way. I know what I saw in my dad’s chart, and what’s there now doesn’t match. I’ve spent the past year trying to prove someone in the clinic system changed it or left parts out, and it’s exhausting, but I don’t think it’s just in my head.
Have you made a formal complaint or accusation to the clinic because of the lab results?

Yes. I’ve been trying for the past year to prove that someone in the clinic system changed or held back parts of my dad’s lab results. I’ve questioned it and pushed them about it, because the chart now doesn’t match what I saw before. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine, but I don’t believe that, and it’s really wearing me down.
Do you generally find it hard to trust other people, even outside of this issue with the clinic?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’m suspicious of everyone, if that’s what you mean. I can usually deal with people fine. This clinic thing is different because of what I saw.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve seen what was in the chart, but not things other people couldn’t see, like… visually. That’s not really what’s happening.
Did this belief start very suddenly, over a few days?

No, not over just a few days. It’s been going on about a year, since my dad’s medical problems started and he needed labs and appointments all the time. That’s when I started noticing things weren’t right.
During this time, have you had periods where you felt very confused about what was real or where your feelings changed very quickly from one moment to the next?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been upset and stressed about it, but I haven’t felt confused about where I was or what was real. My feelings don’t just flip back and forth for no reason, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Because of this belief about the lab results, has your work or day-to-day functioning become seriously impaired?

No, not seriously. I mean, this whole thing takes up a lot of my attention, but outside of arguing about my dad’s records, I still go to my phlebotomy shifts, pay my bills, take care of myself, and handle the normal day-to-day stuff.
